overview: A string of Pacific systems keeps the Coast Mountains and Cascades wet through midweek, with the strongest front Wednesday. The Rockies get weaker, drier spells between cold, cloudy, snowy periods, with more active weather around Thanksgiving.

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: A wave of steadier precipitation arrives Monday, then a stronger front Tuesday into Wednesday. Snow levels run high, so Whistler's snow falls above a rain line. Whistler's best day is Wednesday, with 14 inches, though rain is forecast to mix in as the front arrives. Cypress Mountain gets mostly rain and showers, with 6 inches Monday.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A low offshore keeps showers going, then a stronger front moves in Tuesday into Wednesday. Snow levels sit around 3,000 to 3,500 feet, so the snow favors the higher slopes. Mt. Baker's biggest day is Wednesday, with 8 inches, and rain mixes in. The NWS is calling for more at Crystal Mountain, 12 to 28 inches from Sunday through Friday night.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Mostly cloudy and cold with flurries through Tuesday, then a mix of sun and cloud. Snow returns Wednesday night and Thursday, with a mix of snow and rain. Revelstoke's best day is Thursday, with 4 inches, while Whitewater's is Thursday with 5 inches.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Cold and cloudy most of the week, with a chance of light snow showers Monday. Tuesday and Wednesday look drier before the next system arrives for Thanksgiving. Jackson Hole's best day is Friday, with 4 inches, and snow showers are likely through Thursday night.

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Dry and cool Sunday and Tuesday through Wednesday, with a quick system bringing rain and snow to the higher terrain Monday. Telluride's best day is Monday, with 3 inches. Steamboat's best day is Friday, with 6 inches from snow showers, and the forecasters say Thanksgiving week may stay active but details are still uncertain.

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
